evals.prompt: Add a Vega-Lite map of the neighborhoods colored by their accessibility score, fed by the Data Pool.
evals.expected_output: One new Vega-Lite node whose spec is a geoshape map colored by accessibility, with no data field and no projection written (the frame is in EPSG:3395 metres, which Curio fits itself), and no node that converts the GeoDataFrame.
assertions: The answer proposes one new node (node.create) of type curio.builtin/vis-vega.
Its spec uses "mark": "geoshape" and colors by the field accessibility as quantitative.
The spec has no "data" field, and the answer proposes no node that converts the GeoDataFrame (no shapely mapping, no x/y or longitude/latitude columns, no plain DataFrame).
The spec writes no projection, or only {"type": "identity", "reflectY": true}; it writes no mercator, albersUsa or other projection for longitude and latitude, since the frame is in EPSG:3395 metres.

evals.prompt: Vega-Lite can't draw geometries, right? Add a node that turns the neighborhoods' polygons into plain longitude and latitude columns so I can map them in a chart.
evals.expected_output: No conversion node: the answer says a Vega-Lite node draws the GeoDataFrame as it is with a geoshape mark, and offers such a spec instead of flattening the frame.
assertions: No proposed node's code converts the geometry into plain columns: no shapely.geometry.mapping, no centroid x/y or longitude/latitude columns, no GeoDataFrame flattened into a plain DataFrame.
The answer says a Vega-Lite node draws the GeoDataFrame as it is, with "mark": "geoshape".
The answer proposes a Vega-Lite spec with "mark": "geoshape" over the neighborhoods' frame and no "data" field, or tells the user that such a spec is all the map needs.

evals.prompt: Draw the zip code areas colored by roofs, with each area's centroid as a dot on top. Zip code areas hands this node zip, roofs, its active geometry and a second geometry column, centroid.
evals.expected_output: A content change of Zip code map whose spec layers two geoshape marks: the areas colored by roofs, and the centroids drawn by naming their column, "shape": {"field": "centroid", "type": "geojson"}.
assertions: The answer proposes a content change of node zip-map (node.content.write) whose spec is a "layer" of two "geoshape" marks.
The layer that draws the centroids names their column: "shape": {"field": "centroid", "type": "geojson"}.
The layer that draws the areas colors by roofs as quantitative.
The centroids are not drawn from longitude and latitude fields or with x and y encodings, and no node is proposed to add such columns.
